apiUrl.label: API URL
apiUrl.help: Base URL of the TrueNAS middleware API. Include /api/v2.0.

apiKey.label: API key
apiKey.help: API key generated from Credentials → Local Users → <user> → API Keys. Stored encrypted at rest by the host's encryption service.

datasetPath.label: Dataset path
datasetPath.help: Path to the ZFS dataset to snapshot. Snapshots are taken recursively, covering child datasets.

verifyTls.label: Verify TLS
verifyTls.help: Disable to accept self-signed certificates (default TrueNAS installs). Off is equivalent to --insecure.

form.recursiveHint: Snapshots are recursive: a snapshot of tank/backups covers tank/backups/child1 and tank/backups/child2. The host issues one snapshot per backup run; no child datasets are snapshotted individually.

setup.title: Before you start
setup.intro: snapshot-truenas talks to the TrueNAS middleware API over HTTPS. Confirm the API is reachable from the host, then fill in the form.

steps.title: Confirm the TrueNAS middleware is reachable
steps.body: From the host where McHarbor runs, verify HTTPS connectivity. Replace nas.local with your TrueNAS hostname:

steps.title: Create a dedicated user (recommended)
steps.body: Credentials → Local Users → Add. Grant only the datasets that should be snapshotted. Service-account isolation makes the API key safe to revoke later.

steps.title: Generate an API key
steps.body: Credentials → Local Users → <user> → API Keys → Add. Copy the generated key — TrueNAS only shows it once. Paste it into the API key field on the form.

steps.title: Identify or create the dataset
steps.body: Storage → Pools → ⋮ → Add Dataset. Use a dedicated dataset (e.g. tank/backups) so snapshot churn doesn't bloat the dataset list. Note the exact path — it is case-sensitive.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.body: After saving the configuration, click 'Test Connection' in the Snapshots tab. A green probe result confirms the API key works and the dataset exists on the TrueNAS side.
